meta.source: World Economic Forum, The Future of Jobs Report 2025 (January 2025). Survey of over 1,000 employers across 22 industry clusters and 55 economies, projecting 2025 to 2030.
meta.status: Verified against the report PDF (WEF_Future_of_Jobs_Report_2025.pdf, from Paul's Google Drive) on 2026-09-13. Wording in claims and labels follows the report; figure and section references point to where each item was read.
notes: Cluster typicalTasks are Task Map's starting point for the opening question, not report findings. They carry their own flag.
taskCategories are Task Map's grouping. The evidence each one cites is verified; the grouping is ours.
Skill 'trend' is derived from the net-increase ranking in Figure 3.4: ranks 1 to 20 rising, 21 to 25 flat, 26 (the only net negative) declining.
meta.licensingNote: Confirm WEF terms of use for citing the report inside a product. Attribution is expected.

headline.claim: In the next five years, 170 million jobs are projected to be created, equivalent to 14% of today's total employment.
headline.ref: Figure 2.1, Global employment change by 2030; Executive summary

headline.claim: 92 million current jobs are projected to be displaced, or 8% of total employment.
Net growth of 78 million jobs, 7% of today's total employment.
Job creation and displacement together represent a structural labour market churn of 22% of today's formal jobs.
Employers expect 39% of workers' core skills to change by 2030, down from 44% in the 2023 edition.
Employers in the United Kingdom expect 33% of skills to change by 2030, below the global average of 39%.

Compared to the 2023 edition, leadership and social influence, resilience, flexibility and agility, and AI and big data saw the largest increases in the share of employers calling them core skills: 22, 17 and 17 percentage points respectively. Dependability, attention to detail and quality control decreased in importance.
Skills gaps are considered the biggest barrier to business transformation, with 63% of employers identifying them as a major barrier over 2025 to 2030.
85% of employers surveyed plan to prioritise upskilling their workforce.
70% of employers expect to hire staff with new skills, and 40% plan to reduce staff as their skills become less relevant.
Employers estimate that today 47% of work tasks are performed mainly by humans alone, 22% mainly by technology, and 30% by a combination.

By 2030 employers expect work tasks to be nearly evenly split: about a third each for humans, technology, and a combination. Nearly 82% of the reduction in the human share is attributed to automation, 19% to expanded human-machine collaboration.

Graphic Designers and Legal Secretaries appearing just outside the top ten fastest-declining roles, a first for the report, may illustrate GenAI's increasing capacity to perform knowledge work. In the 2023 edition Graphic Designers were considered a moderately growing job.
Broadening digital access, AI and information processing technologies, and robots and autonomous systems are the primary drivers of the decline in clerical roles.

drivers.label: Rising cost of living, higher prices or inflation
Increased efforts and investments to reduce carbon emissions
Increased focus on labour and social issues
Increased efforts and investments to adapt to climate change

skills.label: Manual dexterity, endurance and precision
skills.ref: Figures 3.3 and 3.4 (the only skill with a net decrease)

taskCategories.label: Information and data processing
taskCategories.note: Reporting, data entry, reconciliation, collation. Data Entry Clerks and Accounting, Bookkeeping and Payroll Clerks are in the fastest-declining list; AI and information processing technologies are a primary driver of clerical decline.

taskCategories.label: Routine administration and scheduling
taskCategories.note: Diary, rota, inbox triage, form filling. Administrative Assistants and Executive Secretaries are in both declining lists.

taskCategories.label: Written communication and drafting
taskCategories.note: First drafts, summaries, replies. The report ties the first-time decline of Legal Secretaries and Graphic Designers to GenAI's capacity for knowledge work. Judgment and voice stay with the person.

taskCategories.label: Analysis and decision support
taskCategories.note: Analytical thinking is the top core skill at 69% and still rising. The tools change what the analysis is done with, not who owns the conclusion.

taskCategories.label: Customer and stakeholder interaction
taskCategories.note: Service orientation and empathy are top-ten core skills, yet Client Information and Customer Service Workers are in the largest-decline list. Routine query handling is exposed; relationship and escalation work is not.

taskCategories.label: People management and coaching
taskCategories.note: Leadership and social influence saw the largest rise of any core skill since 2023 (22 points). Talent management and empathy are core and rising.

taskCategories.label: Physical and on-site work
taskCategories.note: Farmworkers, delivery drivers, construction trades, nursing and personal care lead the largest-growth list. Manual dexterity is the only skill with a net decline in importance, which reflects where employers see technology going, not where these jobs are going by 2030.

taskCategories.label: Creative and design work
taskCategories.note: Creative thinking is core skill number four and rising skill number four, while Graphic Designers appear in both declining lists. Concept stays human; production is exposed.

taskCategories.label: Judgment with accountability
taskCategories.note: Sign-offs, compliance calls, safeguarding, hiring decisions. The person is answerable, whatever the tool suggested. Grouping is Task Map's; the report does not isolate this category.

findings.claim: 56% of companies operating in the United Kingdom anticipate their business being transformed by increased investments in climate adaptation, a higher share than their global peers.
56% of UK employers expect geoeconomic fragmentation to impact their business strategy, compared to 34% globally.
UK respondents expect rising demand for technological literacy, AI and big data, and resilience, flexibility and agility.
Key job roles anticipated to see significant growth in the UK by 2030 include Big Data Specialists, FinTech Engineers, and AI and Machine Learning Specialists.
Employers in the United Kingdom expect 33% of skills to change by 2030, against a global average of 39%.

clusters.label: Operations and general management
clusters.wefEvidence: General and Operations Managers are among the fifteen largest-growth jobs (Figure 2.4) and are named among the roles driving the most net job growth. Business Services and Administration Managers are in the largest-decline list. Growth is in roles that run the operation, not roles that administer it.

clusters.label: Administration and executive support
clusters.wefEvidence: Both roles appear in the fastest-declining list (Figure 2.2) and the largest-decline list (Figure 2.4). The report names broadening digital access, AI and information processing technologies, and robots and autonomous systems as the primary drivers of clerical decline.

clusters.label: Finance, bookkeeping and payroll
clusters.wefEvidence: Accounting, Bookkeeping and Payroll Clerks appear in both declining lists; Accountants and Auditors appear in the largest-decline list (Figure 2.4) and are named by the report among the fastest-declining roles alongside clerical work.

clusters.label: Customer service and support
wefJobs: Client Information and Customer Service Workers
clusters.wefEvidence: Client Information and Customer Service Workers appear in the largest-decline list (Figure 2.4), while service orientation and customer service remains a top-ten core skill (Figure 3.3). Routine handling is exposed; the human service layer is valued.
typicalTasks: Inbound queries by phone, email and chat

clusters.label: Sales and account management
wefJobs: Door-To-Door Sales Workers, News and Street Vendors, and Related Workers
clusters.wefEvidence: Shop Salespersons are in the largest-growth list (Figure 2.4); Telemarketers and Door-To-Door Sales Workers are in the fastest-declining list (Figure 2.2). Relationship selling grows, scripted outreach declines.

clusters.label: HR, learning and talent
clusters.wefEvidence: Talent management is core skill nine (47%) and rising skill eight (Figures 3.3 and 3.4). Teaching and mentoring is rising. 85% of employers plan to prioritise upskilling and 63% call skills gaps the biggest barrier to transformation.

clusters.label: Marketing, content and design
clusters.wefEvidence: Graphic Designers appear in both declining lists, a first for the report, which it links to GenAI's capacity for knowledge work; in the 2023 edition they were a moderately growing job. Creative thinking is core skill four and rising skill four. Marketing and media is rising slowly. Production is exposed; strategy and concept are not.

clusters.label: Software, data and AI
clusters.wefEvidence: All four are in the fastest-growing list (Figure 2.2); Software and Applications Developers are also third in the largest-growth list (Figure 2.4). AI and big data is the fastest-rising skill. The UK profile names Big Data Specialists, FinTech Engineers and AI and Machine Learning Specialists as key growth roles.

clusters.label: Project and programme management
clusters.wefEvidence: Project Managers are in the largest-growth list (Figure 2.4) and are named among the roles driving the most net job growth.

clusters.label: Health and social care
clusters.wefEvidence: All three are in the largest-growth list (Figure 2.4). The report attributes growth in nursing to technology trends and to ageing and declining working-age populations.

clusters.label: Teaching and training
clusters.wefEvidence: Both are in the largest-growth list (Figure 2.4). Teaching and mentoring is a rising skill (Figure 3.4).

clusters.label: Logistics, warehousing and driving
wefJobs: Light Truck or Delivery Services Drivers
clusters.wefEvidence: Light Truck or Delivery Services Drivers are in both growth lists and Car, Van and Motorcycle Drivers in the largest-growth list; Material-Recording and Stock-Keeping Clerks and Transportation Attendants and Conductors are in both declining lists. The moving stays human, the recording does not.

clusters.label: Retail and frontline service
clusters.wefEvidence: Shop Salespersons and Food and Beverage Serving Workers are in the largest-growth list; Cashiers and Ticket Clerks top the largest-decline list (Figure 2.4).

clusters.label: Legal, claims and compliance
clusters.wefEvidence: All three are in the fastest-declining list (Figure 2.2). The report singles out Legal Secretaries as a first-time entry it links to GenAI's capacity for knowledge work.

clusters.label: Senior leadership
clusters.wefEvidence: General and Operations Managers grow; Business Services and Administration Managers are in the largest-decline list (Figure 2.4). Leadership and social influence is core skill three and saw the largest rise of any skill since 2023.
